title: Using custom SV Battler Animation Frames

posts.author: Charon
posts.body:
Sorry for the confusing and and rather cllunky title but I have no Idea how to put my question in a short sentence.
So here is the setting:
I want to use SV Battle, but I dont want to use the SV_Actors spriteheet for the different animations but use custom animations with multiple frames.
So for example: I know how to draw a sprite sheet and how it works. But I dont want the idle animation to only consist of 3 looping frames but multiple looping frames (for example: draw a knife, balance it on a finger, throw it in the air, catch it and put it away, have a few breathing frames and start anew). I can do the frames, but I struggle to implement them.
Of course I also want to do the other "sprite sheet format categories" like Chant, abnormal,... as custom multi-frame animations.
Furthermore, I also want combat skills to play a custom animation that does not "just" use the original sprite and offsets it a bit for jumping, rotates it 360° for a flip and then flashes a sword frame for the attack, but an actual multi frame custom animation with multiple frames for jumping, flipping, landing and slashing.
I assume I will need a plugin for that if it is possible at all.
Can anyone please point me in the right direction?

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
there are basically two different aspects to your description:
more frames
more sequences
more frames is relatively easy and there should already be plugins to enable that.
more sequences is anything but easy.
the problem is that the engine needs to know when to use which motion sequence, so that has to be programmed into the engine.
And that requires a much more extensive change in the engine itself, as each new battler sequence needs to be defined and declared before the artist can make it.
and the programmer and artist have to agree what the new sequences are, where they are stored and so on.
it can be done, but it will require a lot of work - custom work at that.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Something that will help you - both in searching and discussion - is to clear up some of the terminology.
The movements of the SV battlers - chant, abnormal, etc. - are correctly called motions.
Then animations are things defined in the animations tab of your database.
Charon said:
I dont want to use the SV_Actors spriteheet for the different animations but use custom animations with multiple frames.
Click to expand...
This idea is a pretty over-complicated way to do it. There are plugins that simply allow you to define more frames for the different motions on an SV battler spritesheet.
At least, there were for MV and there are for character sprites for MZ, so I'm assuming there's an MZ equivalent for Yami's Sideview Battlers. Or, since it doesn't use any window code, it could even be compatible.

posts.author: Canned_Dinosaur
posts.body:
If it's purely sprite-based with more frames that you want... I am using BattleMotionMZ.js by Lib. It works by just adding additional motions. So the standard spritesheet covers up to index 17, and this plugin can add more in sets of six. Each motion will have a color code as its final cell, with red meaning no loop, green meaning ping-pong loop, and yellow meaning one-way loop.
Downside is that all your spritesheets will have to conform to the same layout, which can mean that some sprites with fewer frames per motion will have lots of blank space... so I suppose you may want to combine it with a preloader if you end up having really huge spritesheets.
The plugin:
